verdict: clear: provider-scoped global search, cumulative pagination/cancellation and phone caller lifecycle reviewed; final captions corrected
review_notes: Only eligible searchable VOD providers participate; M3U/live and browse-only entries are explicitly excluded from the searchable count. The default API backend always supplies category=null.

One bounded worker pool schedules all24 configured eligible sources in the initial batch; subsequent batches request only remaining source cursors. Successful cursors advance, failed pages remain retryable, canceled unfinished requests resume without rescanning successful providers, and stale rounds/keywords cannot append results.

Results retain provider identity and source-local IDs. Same IDs across different providers remain separate; phone cards always display the actual provider name, and detail fetches use the selected Video provider.
Filtered empty raw pages preserve hasMore; repeated nonempty pages stop explicitly. The 2000-item cap is visible and does not skip tail providers in the current batch.

Phone delivery uses asynchronous main.post. Page/detail tickets, cancelRound, foreground/detail guards and close() isolate delayed replies; returning from details resumes cached unfinished search. Separate live-channel search remains available.
The final caption correctly distinguishes all-source failure from no matches and does not offer an impossible failed-source retry after the visible result cap.

Independent tests compile the actual helper plus actual CatalogApi/models and format/category helpers with the JDK, without compile stubs or real network. Full34-Java SDK compilation and597 owner assertions provide complementary caller evidence; no real-device rendering or playback claim is made.
